reviewed_explanations.Explain which malformed, incomplete or u: TestSubjectUnmarshalPreservesReceiverOnFailure drives 11 inputs through the real production decoder via json.Unmarshal into a receiver pre-populated with the shared identity testUUID/testCommit/testTreeDigest and asserts receiver == original after each rejection (whole-struct equality covers all three fields and any future field): empty input; array instead of object; truncated object (syntax error); non-string tree_digest (true); missing commit; missing tree_digest; unknown field 'unexpected'; duplicated resource_id member; invalid resource_id 'not-a-uuid'; invalid commit 'abc123'; invalid tree_digest 'sha256:zzzz'. Together they exercise each rejection family the decoder implements: non-object/trailing syntax, JSON type error, each required-field absence, unknown field, duplicate member, and each of the three semantic validators. TestSubjectUnmarshalReplacesReceiverOnSuccess supplies a fully valid document whose every value differs from the pre-existing identity (22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222 vs 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111; fedcba98... vs 01234567...; sha256:0000... vs sha256:0123...) and asserts receiver == replacement plus explicit per-field inequality against the original. A receiver that was never written would still hold the original identity and fail that assertion, so preservation on failure is demonstrated as conditional validated-then-assigned behavior, not as an inert decoder that ignores every input. The file is a new, explicitly scoped test; daemon/internal/protocol/goal_subject.go and every baseline Go test are unmodified in this revision.
reviewed_explanations.Explain why assigning the decoded Subjec: Subject.UnmarshalJSON (daemon/internal/protocol/goal_subject.go:51-62) decodes into a function-local subjectWire, converts it into a local Subject, runs value.Validate(), and only then executes the single statement *subject = value. Every failure return precedes that one assignment: decodeStrictObject rejects empty/whitespace input and non-object values, rejects duplicate members through RejectDuplicateJSONMembers, rejects a missing required field, rejects unknown fields through decoder.DisallowUnknownFields plus json type errors, and rejects trailing data through ensureDecoderEOF; value.Validate() then rejects a bad resource_id, commit or tree_digest. No code path assigns subject.ResourceID, subject.Commit or subject.TreeDigest individually, so the receiver cannot be half-updated: it changes atomically from the caller's previous bytes to a fully validated value, or it does not change at all. Decoding straight into the receiver (json.Unmarshal(data, subject)) would write field by field, and Go's encoding/json keeps assigning later members after an earlier member error, so a caller could observe a partially mutated Subject even though the call returned an error. Sealed evidence: protocol-tests stdout sha256:58107cf6... with validator stdout sha256:17ef5047... printing 'verified TestSubjectUnmarshalPreservesReceiverOnFailure: run=1 pass=1 skip=0' and the same line for TestSubjectUnmarshalReplacesReceiverOnSuccess (assert-go-test-json.py requires run=1, pass=1, skip=0, no skipped descendants), inside attempt-0001 sha256:38ad6dee..., bound to subject sha256:b14e8469....

reviewer_findings.description: No action required. The 11 rejection sub-cases assert only that decoding returns an error plus whole-struct receiver preservation, not which guard rejected. Two sub-cases are not uniquely attributable: 'missing commit' and 'missing tree digest' would still fail through Subject.Validate() if decodeStrictObject's required-field check were removed, because the zero value fails validateGitObjectID/validateSHA256. The frozen outcome required preservation on rejection and full replacement on success (not error identity), and the remaining sub-cases do pin their guards (removing RejectDuplicateJSONMembers, DisallowUnknownFields, the object check or ensureDecoderEOF makes the corresponding input decode successfully and the test fail).
